metadata.description: Wire format for the final `vibe <phase> --json` lifecycle report. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/lifecycle_report/`.
Always `"lifecycle"` for this report.
The exact default-lifecycle phase requested by the user.

The REQUESTED full chain: every phase spelling this invocation set out to run, in order, including a leading `clean` when the clean lifecycle was composed. It does not shrink when the run stops early.

The ACTUALLY EXECUTED prefix of `chain`, in the same order — one outcome per phase that ran. A completed run reports every phase in `chain`; a run that parked for a hosting agent ends at the phase whose status is `delegated`, and the phases after it are absent because they did not run.
Effective lifecycle contributions in canonical execution order with their execution outcomes.
Non-fatal collection notices that must remain observable in structured output.
Present exactly when the invocation parked an agent execution for the hosting agent. Human/quiet rendering consumes the same value as the typed member.
The shared compile-trace member (PROP-054 `##OBS-TRACE`, R3.4): present exactly when this command ran with compile tracing enabled; disabled old JSON omits it and remains readable.
Honest handler outcome such as `ok`, `fail`, or `skip`.
True when a durable operation completed but this contribution left it requiring attention.
Structured handler message. Human mode may render it; JSON mode never leaks it outside this document.
Authored source reference for a synthetic or translated lifecycle contribution.
Package slot whose pre/post-install timing event this contribution targeted.
Bounded UTF-8 lossy capture of script stdout for structured lifecycle reports, at most 1 MiB. Binary stdout is the reply protocol and is never stored here.
Bounded UTF-8 lossy capture of handler stderr for structured lifecycle reports, at most 1 MiB.
True when stdout exceeded the 1 MiB structured-report bound and was truncated.
True when stderr exceeded the 1 MiB structured-report bound and was truncated.
Phase outcome vocabulary. R2.4 writes `ok`, `fresh`, or `no-op`; the first handler failure aborts the chain. R7.3 adds `delegated`: the chain parked at this phase and later phases did not run.
The durable run identity the hosting agent resumes under.
Ordered project-relative outbox task files awaiting the hosting agent.
The exact command that resumes this run (`vibe <requested-phase>`).
